ॐ

Mahānyāsam

Bodhāyana's great placing · Rudra's nyāsa, ablution and worship

The complete Mahānyāsa as printed in one Telugu edition: the five placings of Rudra's mantras on the body, the Rudra ablution and worship, the elevenfold Rudrābhiṣeka with the ten peace-chants and the imperial anointing, the worship of Śiva with the Mṛtyuñjaya-mānasa-pūjā verses, and the Mahāśivarātri arghyas. The Vedic mantras carry their accents — anudātta ॒ below, svarita ॑ above, dīrgha svarita ᳚ — shown in the Devanāgarī, in which this page opens, and in the Telugu; the IAST is an unaccented reading aid. The Sanskrit keeps the book's readings, its Taittirīya spelling (gṃ) and its abbreviations (…); the edition's Telugu instructions are not reproduced — the directions are short original English notes.

Mahānyāsa prayogaḥ · the great placing ↑

Bodhāyana's Mahānyāsa: before worshipping Rudra the worshipper becomes Rudra, placing (nyāsa) Rudra's mantras on his own body — only one who is Rudra should worship Rudra. The page follows one printed tradition in full; Vedic mantras carry their svaras (shown in Devanāgarī). Where a nyāsa mantra ends with a limb ('śikhāyai namaḥ', 'to the crest'), touch that limb.

oṃ śivāya gurave namaḥ

word by word · translation

om om śivāya to Śiva gurave the teacher namaḥ salutation

Oṃ. Salutation to Śiva, the teacher.

Pañcāṅga Rudra dhyānam · the five-limbed Rudra ↑

The five mantras of the Pañcākṣarī (na-ma-śi-vā-ya), each with a verse, a Vedic mantra and a group of letters, are placed on the five 'limbs' of Rudra.

hariḥ Hari om om namaḥ salutation bhagavate to the blessed rudrāya Rudra atha now ataḥ then pañca-aṅga-rudrāṇām of the Rudras of the five limbs

Hari Oṃ. Salutation to the Lord Rudra. Now, the five limbs of Rudra.

Oṃ, the three worlds; the seed 'maṃ'. Salutation to the Lord of the end and to the ender of the Lord of the end; to the upward one and the upward liṅga; the golden one and the golden liṅga; the gleaming one and the gleaming liṅga; the divine one and the divine liṅga; Bhava and Bhava's liṅga; Śarva and Śarva's liṅga; Śiva and Śiva's liṅga; the blazing one and the blazing liṅga; the Self and the Self-liṅga; the supreme and the supreme liṅga. This establishes every liṅga of moon and sun, the pure mantra of the hand. — Letters ca to ña; 'maṃ' oṃ; salutation to Rudra of the southern limb.

Pañcamukha dhyānam · the five faces ↑

Each of the five faces — east, south, west, north and upward — with its Brahma-mantra, a verse of meditation, and the placing of its letters.

Oṃ, 'naṃ'. May we know the supreme Person, meditate on the Great God; may Rudra impel us.

For the Haṃsa Gāyatrī: the seer is the Self, the deity the Supreme Self, the metre the unmanifest Gāyatrī, applied in its recitation. The syllables 'haṃ sāṃ' to 'haṃ saḥ' are placed on the fingers and on the heart, head, crest, armour, eyes and weapon; bhūr bhuvas suvar oṃ binds the quarters.

Meditation. I see and bow to the Haṃsa, form of the Supreme Self: abiding in coming and going, void as the sky, lamp of consciousness that dispels the dark, dwelling within all people. The body is called the temple, the living being the eternal god; cast off the faded offering of ignorance and worship in the thought 'I am He'.

The Haṃsa mantra: haṃsa, haṃsa, paramahaṃsa, so'ham, haṃsa so'ham haṃsa. May we know the Haṃsa, meditate on the Paramahaṃsa; may the Haṃsa impel us. Whoever says 'haṃsa haṃsa' — Sadāśiva is named Haṃsa. Having done this placing, he begins the enclosure.

Digdevatā nyāsaḥ · the guardians of the ten quarters ↑

Each quarter's mantra is 'enclosed' (sampuṭa): the praṇava, the three worlds and the seed-syllable before it, the salutation to Rudra and the seed after it; then the guardian of that quarter is saluted.

Ṣoḍaśāṅga raudrīkaraṇam · the sixteen limbs made Rudra ↑

śikhāśiraścamūrdhā ca lalāṭaṃ netrakarṇakau | mukhaṃ ca kaṃṭhabāhū ca hṛnnābhī ca kaṭi stathā |
ūrūjānū jaṃghapādau ṣoḍaśāṃga sthalāni vai ||

word by word · translation

śikhā top-knot śiraḥ head ca and mūrdhā crown ca and lalāṭam forehead netra-karṇakau eyes and ears mukham mouth ca and kaṇṭha-bāhū throat and arms ca and hṛt-nābhī heart and navel ca and kaṭiḥ waist tathā likewise ūrū-jānū thighs and knees jaṅghā-pādau shanks and feet ṣoḍaśa-aṅga-sthalāni are the sixteen places of the limbs vai indeed

Crest, head and crown, forehead, eyes and ears, mouth, throat and arms, heart, navel and hips, thighs, knees, shanks and feet: these are the sixteen places.

Sixteen Agni formulas ('you are …; with the Rudra-host protect me, Agni; fill me, do not harm me'), each enclosed with a vowel as seed, placed on sixteen parts of the body.

tato bhūtapretapiśāca baddha brahmarākṣasa yakṣa yamadūta śākinī ḍhākinī sarpa śvāpada taskara jvarādyupa drava jopaghātāssarve jvalaṃtaṃ māṃ (yajamānaṃ) paśyaṃtu māṃ rakṣaṃtu yajamānagṃ rakṣaṃtu ||

word by word · translation

tvak-asthi-gataiḥ lodged in skin and bone sarva-pāpaiḥ from all sins pramucyate one is freed sarva-bhūteṣu among all beings aparājitaḥ unconquered bhavati one becomes tataḥ then bhūta-preta-piśāca-baddha-brahmarākṣasa-yakṣa-yamadūta-śākinī-ḍhākinī-sarpa-śvāpada-taskara-jvara-ādi-upadrava-ja-upaghātāḥ harms arising from afflictions such as ghosts, spirits, fiends, brahmarākṣasas, yakṣas, Yama's messengers, witches, serpents, beasts of prey, thieves and fevers sarve all jvalantam blazing mām me yajamānam the sacrificer paśyantu may they see mām me rakṣantu may they protect yajamānam the sacrificer rakṣantu may they protect

He is freed from all sins lodged in skin and bone and is unconquered among all beings. Then may all ghosts, spirits, goblins, bound brahma-rākṣasas, yakṣas, Yama's messengers, śākinīs and ḍākinīs, serpents, beasts of prey, thieves, fevers and every harm see me (the sacrificer) blazing — may they protect me, protect the sacrificer.

Caturtho nyāsaḥ · the fourth placing, self-protection ↑

Five mantras to Agni placed from the privy parts up to the head, a sixth on the head, and the Brāhmaṇa of the 'hotṛs' of the Self, protect the self.

It called within, 'Self, Self!', and the fourth answered it; so it became the Caturhūta, the four-called — that indeed is its name. Him, being Caturhūta, the four-called, they call the Caturhotṛ, indirectly, for the gods love what is indirect. It said to him: 'You heard me nearest; through you they will be told'. Therefore they call them the Caturhotṛs; therefore the son who listens is dearest to the heart. The nearest is dearest; he who knows this becomes nearest to Brahman.

Thus self-protection is to be done: the fourth placing.

Pañcamo nyāsaḥ · the fifth placing, the six limbs ↑

The fifth placing is six-fold: the Śivasaṅkalpa hymn to the heart, the Puruṣa Sūkta to the head, the Uttara-Nārāyaṇa to the crest-lock, the Apratiratha to the armour, 'pratipūruṣam' and 'vibhrāṭ' to the eyes, and 'tvam agne' with the Śatarudrīya as the weapon.

śarma shelter yacchatu may he grant

The Apratiratha hymn: Indra, swift and fearsome as a bull, the stirrer of peoples, roaring, unblinking, the lone hero, conquers a hundred armies at once; with him, the victorious and unshakeable, men conquer. Bṛhaspati flies round with his chariot slaying demons; Indra, leader of the gods' armies with Bṛhaspati, the sacrifice and Soma, and the Maruts going before, raises the battle-cry; the arrow, sharpened by prayer, is sped at the foe. 'Your vital points I cover with armour …'; 'where the arrows fly like boys with loose hair, may Indra the Vṛtra-slayer grant us shelter always'.

The gods and the asuras were at war. The gods saw this Apratiratha, 'the unrivalled', and by it overcame the asuras — hence its name. When the second hotṛ recites it, the sacrificer overcomes his rival and wins what was unwon. It has ten verses; the virāj has ten syllables, and by it the two worlds are held apart; the virāj is food, and in food he stands firm. (Then the stone is set down in the Āgnīdhra.)

The Tryambaka offering and its Brāhmaṇa: cakes on one potsherd are offered to Rudra, one for each person of the house and one over; 'your beast, Rudra, is the mole'; 'this is your portion, Rudra, with your sister Ambikā'; a remedy for cow, horse and man; the Tryambaka verse; 'go beyond the Mūjavat with your bow unstrung'. Then the reasons for each act — the crossroads, the middle leaf, the single firebrand, the offering hung up, going without looking back, the water sprinkled, and the Āditya cake that sets the sacrificer back on the earth. It ends 'May the far-shining one drink the pleasant soma …'.

'You, Agni, are Rudra …'. Gods, go to the gods; the first to the second, the second to the third, and so on to the thirty-third: the gods thrice eleven, thrice three and thirty, be higher, of higher paths and higher power. May the wish for which I offer this be fulfilled; may we be lords of riches. Bhūr bhuvas svaḥ svāhā.

Chest, head, sight, mind, speech, feet, hands and ears — this is called the eight-limbed prostration.

Rudra dhyānam · meditation on Rudra ↑

athātmānagṃ śivātmānagṃ śrīrudrarūpiṇa mevaṃ dhyāyet ||

word by word · translation

atha now ātmānam oneself śiva-ātmānam as one with Śiva śrī-rudra-rūpiṇam in the form of Śrī Rudra evam thus dhyāyet one should meditate on

Then he meditates on himself as Śiva, in the form of Śrī Rudra, thus:

śuddhasphaṭikasaṃkāśaṃ triṇetraṃ paṃcavaktrakam daśabhujagṃ sarvābharaṇabhūṣitaṃ nīlagrīvam śaśāṃkacihnaṃ nāgayajñopavītinaṃ nāgābharaṇa bhūṣitam | vyāghracarmāṃbaradharaṃ kamaṃḍalvakṣa sūtradharam abhayavarakaraṃ śūlahastaṃ jvalaṃtaṃ kapila jaṭājūṭinaṃ śikhā mudyotadhāriṇam ||

word by word · translation

śuddha-sphaṭika-saṅkāśam like pure crystal tri-ṇetram three-eyed pañca-vaktrakam five-faced daśa-bhujam ten-armed sarva-ābharaṇa-bhūṣitam adorned with every ornament nīla-grīvam blue-necked śaśāṅka-cihnam marked with the moon nāga-yajña-upavītinam with a serpent as sacred thread nāga-ābharaṇa-bhūṣitam adorned with serpent ornaments vyāghra-carma-ambara-dharam wearing a tiger skin kamaṇḍalu-akṣa-sūtra-dharam holding water-pot and rosary abhaya-vara-karam with hands granting fearlessness and boons śūla-hastam trident in hand jvalantam blazing kapila-jaṭā-jūṭinam with a mass of tawny locks śikhām a crest udyota-dhāriṇam bearing radiance

Pure as crystal, three-eyed, five-faced, ten-armed, adorned with every ornament, blue-throated, marked with the moon, a serpent for sacred thread and serpents for ornaments, clad in tiger-skin, bearing water-pot and rosary, hands granting fearlessness and boons, trident in hand, blazing, with tawny matted locks and a shining top-knot;

vṛṣaskaṃdha samārūḍha mumādehārdhadhāriṇam | amṛtenāplutaṃhṛṣṭaṃ divyabhogasamanvitam ||

word by word · translation

vṛṣa-skandha-samārūḍham mounted on the bull's shoulder umā-deha-ardha-dhāriṇam bearing Umā as half his body amṛtena with nectar āplutam bathed hṛṣṭam joyful divya-bhoga-samanvitam endowed with divine enjoyments

mounted on the bull's shoulder, Umā as half his body, bathed in nectar, joyful, possessed of divine delights;

digdevatāsamāyuktaṃ surāsura namaskṛtam | nityaṃ ca śāśvataṃ śuddhaṃ dhruvamakṣara mavyayam ||

word by word · translation

dik-devatā-samāyuktam attended by the deities of the quarters sura-asura-namaskṛtam saluted by gods and demons nityam eternal ca and śāśvatam everlasting śuddham pure dhruvam fixed akṣaram imperishable avyayam undecaying

attended by the gods of the quarters, bowed to by gods and demons, eternal, everlasting, pure, fixed, imperishable, undecaying;

sarvavyāpinamīśānaṃ rudraṃ vai viśvarūpiṇam | evaṃ dhyātvā dvijassamyaktato yajanamārabhet ||

word by word · translation

sarva-vyāpinam all-pervading īśānam the ruler rudram Rudra vai indeed viśva-rūpiṇam of every form evam thus dhyātvā having meditated dvijaḥ the twice-born samyak rightly tataḥ then yajanam the worship ārabhet should begin

the all-pervading Lord, Rudra, whose form is the universe — having so meditated, the twice-born should then begin the worship.

Rudra snāna-arcana · the bathing and worship of Rudra ↑

The Rudra-snāna proper: the gods are installed in the body, the god is invoked into the liṅga and worshipped, then bathed with a continuous stream while the Rudra is chanted.

athā'to rudrasnānā'rcanā'bhiṣekavidhiṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ |
udita eva tīrthe snātvo detya śuciḥ prayato brahmacārī śuklavāsāḥ tasya dakṣiṇā pratyagdeśe tanmukhaṃ sthitvā'tmani devatāssthāpayet ||

word by word · translation

atha now ataḥ then rudra-snāna-arcana-abhiṣeka-vidhim the method of Rudra's bath, worship and anointing vyākhyāsyāmaḥ we shall explain udite at sunrise eva itself tīrthe at a holy water snātvā having bathed udetya coming out śuciḥ pure prayataḥ self-controlled brahmacārī celibate śukla-vāsāḥ in white clothes tasya of the deity dakṣiṇā-pratyak-deśe in the south-west tat-mukham facing him sthitvā standing ātmani in himself devatāḥ the deities sthāpayet he should install

Now we shall explain the rite of bathing, worship and ablution of Rudra. At sunrise, having bathed at a holy place and come out, pure, restrained, chaste, in white clothes, standing to the south-west of it and facing it, he installs the gods in himself.

Ātmani devatā-sthāpanam · installing the gods in oneself ↑

prajanane brahma tiṣṭhatu | pādayo rviṣṇu stiṣṭhatu | hastayo rhara stiṣṭhatu |
bāhvo riṃdra stiṣṭhatu | jaṭhare agni stiṣṭhatu | hṛdaye śiva stiṣṭhatu | kaṃṭhe vasava stiṣṭhaṃtu |
vaktre sarasvatī tiṣṭhatu | nāsikayo rvāyu stiṣṭhatu | nayanayo ścaṃdrādityau tiṣṭhetām |
karṇayo raśvinau tiṣṭhetām | lalāṭe rudrā stiṣṭhaṃtu | mūrdhnyā dityā stiṣṭhaṃtu |
śirasi mahādeva stiṣṭhatu | śikhāyāṃ vāmadeva stiṣṭhatu | pṛṣṭhe pinākī tiṣṭhatu |
purata śśūlī tiṣṭhatu | pārśvayo śśivāśaṃkarau tiṣṭhetām | sarvato vāyu stiṣṭhatu |
tato bahissarvato'gnijvālāmālāparivṛtā stiṣṭhaṃtu |
sarveṣvaṃgeṣu sarvā devatāḥ yathāsthānaṃ tiṣṭhaṃtu | māṃ rakṣaṃtu | yajamānagṃ rakṣaṃtu ||
agnirmevāciśrita iti yathā liṃgamaṃgāni sammṛśya ||

word by word · translation

prajanane in the generative organ brahmā Brahmā tiṣṭhatu may he stay pādayoḥ in the feet viṣṇuḥ Viṣṇu tiṣṭhatu may he stay hastayoḥ in the hands haraḥ Hara tiṣṭhatu may he stay bāhvoḥ in the arms indraḥ Indra tiṣṭhatu may he stay jaṭhare in the belly agniḥ Agni tiṣṭhatu may he stay hṛdaye in the heart śivaḥ Śiva tiṣṭhatu may he stay kaṇṭhe in the throat vasavaḥ the Vasus tiṣṭhantu may they stay vaktre in the mouth sarasvatī Sarasvatī tiṣṭhatu may she stay nāsikayoḥ in the nostrils vāyuḥ Vāyu tiṣṭhatu may he stay nayanayoḥ in the eyes candra-ādityau the Moon and the Sun tiṣṭhetām may the two stay karṇayoḥ in the ears aśvinau the Aśvins tiṣṭhetām may the two stay lalāṭe on the forehead rudrāḥ the Rudras tiṣṭhantu may they stay mūrdhni on the crown ādityāḥ the Ādityas tiṣṭhantu may they stay śirasi in the head mahā-devaḥ Mahādeva tiṣṭhatu may he stay śikhāyām in the top-knot vāmadevaḥ Vāmadeva tiṣṭhatu may he stay pṛṣṭhe at the back pinākī the bearer of Pināka tiṣṭhatu may he stay purataḥ in front śūlī the trident-bearer tiṣṭhatu may he stay pārśvayoḥ at the sides śivā-śaṅkarau Śivā and Śaṅkara tiṣṭhetām may the two stay sarvataḥ all around vāyuḥ Vāyu tiṣṭhatu may he stay tataḥ beyond that bahiḥ outside sarvataḥ all around agni-jvālā-mālā-parivṛtāḥ encircled by garlands of flame tiṣṭhantu may they stay sarveṣu in all aṅgeṣu the limbs sarvāḥ all devatāḥ the deities yathā-sthānam each in its place tiṣṭhantu may they stay mām me rakṣantu may they protect yajamānam the sacrificer rakṣantu may they protect agniḥ me vāci śritaḥ “agnir me vāci śritaḥ” iti with this yathā-liṅgam as each verse indicates aṅgāni the limbs sammṛśya having touched

Let Brahmā stand in the organ of generation, Viṣṇu in the feet, Hara in the hands, Indra in the arms, Agni in the belly, Śiva in the heart, the Vasus in the throat, Sarasvatī in the mouth, Vāyu in the nostrils, moon and sun in the eyes, the Aśvins in the ears, the Rudras on the forehead, the Ādityas on the crown, Mahādeva on the head, Vāmadeva in the top-knot, Pinākin behind, the trident-bearer in front, Śiva and Śaṅkara at the sides, Vāyu all around; outside, all around, garlands of flame; let all the gods stand in all my limbs, each in its place — may they protect me, protect the sacrificer. With 'agnir me vāci' he touches the limbs as the words direct.

immortal amṛtam the immortal brahmaṇi in Brahman īśānaḥ Īśāna me in my manyau wrath śritaḥ rests manyuḥ wrath hṛdaye in the heart hṛdayam the heart mayi in me aham I amṛte in the immortal amṛtam the Brahman punaḥ again me to me ātmā the self punaḥ again āyuḥ life ā agāt has returned punaḥ again prāṇaḥ breath punaḥ again ākūtam intent ā agāt has returned vaiśvānaraḥ Vaiśvānara raśmibhiḥ with his rays vāvṛdhānaḥ growing antaḥ within tiṣṭhatu may he stay amṛtasya of immortality gopāḥ the guardian

Fire is set in my speech; speech in the heart; the heart in me; I in the immortal; the immortal in Brahman. So wind in my breath, the sun in my eye, the moon in my mind, the quarters in my ear, the waters in my seed, the earth in my body, plants and trees in my hair, Indra in my strength, Parjanya in my head, Īśāna in my anger, the self in my self. May my self come back to me, my life, my breath, my purpose; may Vaiśvānara, growing with his rays, stand within as guardian of immortality.

om om āśāste hopes ayam this yajamānaḥ sacrificer asau so-and-so āyuḥ for life āśāste he hopes su-prajāḥ-tvam for good offspring āśāste he hopes sajāta-vanasyām for the favour of kinsmen āśāste he hopes uttarām for higher deva-yajyām worship of the gods āśāste he hopes bhūyaḥ for more haviḥ-karaṇam making of oblations āśāste he hopes divyam for the heavenly dhāma abode āśāste he hopes viśvam for all priyam that is dear āśāste he hopes yat what anena by this haviṣā oblation āśāste he hopes for tat that aśyāt may he attain tat in that ṛdhyāt may he prosper tat that asmai to him devāḥ the gods rāsantām may they grant tat that agniḥ Agni devaḥ the god devebhyaḥ from the gods vanate wins vayam we agneḥ from Agni mānuṣāḥ men iṣṭam what is wished ca and vītam what is enjoyed ca and ubhe both ca and naḥ us dyāvā-pṛthivī Heaven and Earth aṃhasaḥ from distress pātām may they protect iha here gatiḥ is the course vāmasya of the good idam this ca and namaḥ homage devebhyaḥ to the gods

This sacrificer, so-and-so, prays: for life, for good offspring, for his kinsmen's goodwill, for a higher worship of the gods, for more offerings, for the heavenly abode, for all that is dear. What he prays for with this offering, may he gain it, may it prosper; may the gods grant it; Agni the god wins it from the gods, and we are Agni's men. What is offered and what is enjoyed — may heaven and earth guard us from distress. Here is the way of the good; salutation to the gods.

The anuvāka 'śaṃ ca me': may happiness and delight be mine, the dear and the desired, good cheer, the fortunate and the better, wealth, fame, fortune and riches, a guide and an upholder, safety and steadiness, all and greatness, understanding and knowing, begetting and birth, the plough and the furrow, right and immortality, freedom from sickness, life and long life, freedom from foes and from fear, easy ways, rest, good dawns and good days. — So the bath of pure water that removes impurity.

First the anuvāka 'śaṃ ca me', then the eleven anuvākas 'namaste rudra manyave', then one anuvāka at a time from 'agnāviṣṇū sajoṣasā'; at every round he worships again, and dismisses with 'vikiridaḥ vilohita'. This is the Rudra-rite, the highest worship: whoever seeks the end of sin, freedom from sickness, life, liberation, fortune, peace, nourishment, contentment, growth, wisdom, intelligence, long life, health or food should do it, and doing so gains success. The priest's fee: ten cows with calves, eleven bulls adorned with gold, gems and jewels; if these cannot be had, one cow — he gains the fruit of a thousand horse-sacrifices and hundred sacrifices, says the revered Bodhāyana.

Thus the Mahānyāsa.

❧

Rudrābhiṣeka · the elevenfold ablution ↑

The ablution is done in eleven rounds. Each round the whole Namaka is chanted with one anuvāka of the Camaka while the liṅga is bathed in an unbroken stream; the round closes with the short worship ('vāmadevāya namaḥ …') and the Rudra-gāyatrī, and the resolve is renewed for the next. After the eleventh come the ten peace-chants and the imperial anointing, and the worship of Śiva below.

Salutation to speech, spoken and unspoken; to the seers who made and own the mantras — may they not forsake me, nor I them. May I speak the speech of all the gods, gracious, delightful to the gods, pleasing to men. Heaven, earth, this whole world, moon and sun, Brahmā and Prajāpati be my shelter. I will speak what is, the world, splendour, fame, austerity, Brahman and truth; for it I spread this covering — may it cover my offspring and cattle. May in-breath and out-breath guard me from death and not forsake me. I will think, beget and speak sweetness; may the gods help me to beauty and the Fathers approve. Peace …

May the wind blow kindly, the sun shine kindly, the days and nights be kind, the dawn break kindly and the sun rise kindly; be gracious, Sarasvatī. Blow here your remedy, wind, blow away what is harmful. I take refuge in Indra's house, in earth, mid-air and heaven, in Prajāpati's Brahman-sheath, in Oṃ. Place in me wisdom, offspring, Agni's splendour, Indra's power, the sun's radiance. Protect us day and night, Aśvins. May the waters be kind; may earth, mid-air, heaven, the quarters, fire, wind, sun, moon, stars, waters, plants, trees, cattle, goats, horses, man, Brahman and the brāhmaṇa be peace — peace itself; may peace be mine, and with it I make peace for my two-footed and four-footed. May Śrī, modesty, steadiness, austerity, wisdom, firmness, faith, truth and dharma not leave me. May we see a hundred autumns … May the red-eyed sun that rose from the ocean purify me. Hold for me what I know; may it not slip away. Wisdom and insight, enter me. Brahman we have spoken; may it not forsake us. Peace …

You are Mitra, you are Varuṇa; I am one with all the gods. You are the navel of rule, its womb; sit on the pleasant seat, the good seat; let it not harm you, nor me. At the impulse of god Savitṛ, with the Aśvins' arms and Pūṣan's hands, with the Aśvins' healing I anoint you for splendour and holy lustre; with Sarasvatī's healing for strength and food; with Indra's power for fortune, fame and might.

These songs to Rudra of the firm bow, swift arrows and self-reliance, unconquered and conquering, bountiful, sharp-weaponed — bring them, listen. With your most healing remedies, Rudra, may I reach a hundred winters; drive far hatred, sin and every sickness. Harm us not in our children; may the favour of the Maruts' father come; keep us not from the sight of the sun; may our hero prevail among horses; may we have offspring, Rudra. Be not angry, bull, nor harm us; hear us here; may we speak loud in the assembly with brave sons. May Rudra's weapon pass us by. You, Agni, are Rudra, the king of the rite.

Praise him with the good arrows and good bow, who rules every remedy; worship Rudra for favour, the mighty god, with salutations. This hand of mine is fortunate, more fortunate; this is my all-healing, this my gentle touch. The thousand, ten thousand snares of death to slay mortals — by the power of the sacrifice we remove them all. Svāhā to death, to death. You are the knot of the breaths; Rudra, enter me as the ender; with this food be strengthened. Salutation to Rudra, to Viṣṇu; guard me from death. Peace …

||

'To the tamer of all beings' — food; 'candramā manaso jātaḥ …'; 'yā te hetiḥ …'. Verses offering the royal rice, sweet and soft, in a ruby bowl, with asafoetida, cumin, pepper and many fine vegetables, with cakes and dal, fresh ghee; milk-rice with sugar and banana; sweet pāyasa with cardamom and pepper; banana pieces with mustard and cumin; āmalaka, wood-apple and lotus-stalk with salt; curd-rice with cardamom and ginger in a golden bowl; ginger with lime and green mango; buttermilk with dry ginger and asafoetida; cool, sweet, clear water. Sprinkling with the Gāyatrī: 'I sprinkle truth with right'.

At Mṛtyuñjaya's feet I lay a handful of punnāga, blue lily, jasmine, mandāra, oleander and lotus with bilva and tulasī; 'sahasraśīrṣaṃ devam … sadāśivom'. — I offer flowers with mantras.

Lord adorned with the serpent-king, I give arghya again at the lotus feet of Mṛtyuñjaya, praised by Brahmā and the gods, marked with lotus, fish and discus. — I offer arghya again.

om om īśānaḥ “īśānaḥ” iti with this pradakṣiṇa-namaskārān circumambulation and prostrations pade pade at every step sarva-tamaḥ-nikṛntanam cutting away all darkness pade pade at every step sarva-śubha-pradāyakam giving every good pradakṣiṇam circumambulation bhakti-yutena full of devotion cetasā with a mind karomi I perform mṛtyuñjaya O conqueror of death rakṣa rakṣa protect, protect mām me yāni kāni whatever ca and pāpāni sins mahā-īśvara O great Lord śrī Śrī bhavānī Bhavānī śaṅkara and Śaṅkara devatābhyaḥ to the deities namaḥ salutation ātma-pradakṣiṇa-trayam three turnings about oneself samarpayāmi I offer

'īśāna' — circumambulations and salutations. With a devoted heart I walk round you, Mṛtyuñjaya — each step cutting away all darkness, each step giving every good; protect me, protect me. 'yāni kāni ca pāpāni … maheśvara'. — I offer three circumambulations.

'īśānaḥ sarvavidyānām' — salutations; 'yajñena yajñam …'. Salutation to Gaurī's lord, white as crystal; salutation to the lord of the worlds, praised by the gods; salutation to the blue-throated one who destroyed the city-demons; salutation to the forehead-eyed destroyer of Love's pride. — I offer salutations.

śrīmṛtyuṃjaya pārvatīpriya sadā māṃ pāhi sarveśvara ||

karoti pratyūṣe niśidivasamadhye ca sapumān

śrī bhavānīśaṃkara devatābhyo namaḥ kṣamāyācana pūrvaka prārthanaṃ samarpayāmi ||

garva-andham blind with pride bahu-pāpa-varga-sahitam laden with many kinds of sin kāruṇya-dṛṣṭyā with a glance of compassion vibho O Lord śrī-mṛtyuñjaya Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya pārvatī-priya beloved of Pārvatī sadā always mām me pāhi protect sarva-īśvara lord of all saudhe in a palace ratna-maye made of gems nava-utpala-dala-ākīrṇe strewn with fresh lily petals catuṣka-antare within the hall kauśeyena with silk manaḥ-hareṇa charming dhavalena white ācchādite covered sarvaśaḥ all over karpūra-añcita-dīpa-dīpti-milite lit by camphor lamps ramya-upadhāna-dvaye with two lovely pillows pārvatyāḥ of Pārvatī kara-padma-lālita-padam whose feet are caressed by the lotus hands mṛtyuñjayam Mṛtyuñjaya bhāvaye I contemplate catuḥ-catvāriṃśat forty-four vilasat-upacāraiḥ with splendid services abhimataiḥ desired manaḥ-padme in the lotus of the mind bhaktyā with devotion bahiḥ outwardly api also ca and pūjām worship śubha-karām auspicious karoti performs pratyūṣe at dawn niśi at night divasa-madhye at midday ca and saḥ that pumān man prayāti goes to śrī-mṛtyuñjaya-padam the abode of Śrī Mṛtyuñjaya aneka-adbhuta-padam the abode of many wonders prātaḥ at dawn liṅgam the liṅga umā-pateḥ of the lord of Umā ahaḥ ahaḥ day after day sandarśanāt by being seen svarga-dam gives heaven madhya-ahne at midday haya-medha-tulya-phala-dam gives fruit equal to a horse-sacrifice sāyantane in the evening mokṣa-dam gives liberation bhānoḥ of the sun astamaye at the setting pradoṣa-samaye at the time of dusk pañca-akṣara-ārādhanam worship with the five syllables tat-kāla-traya-tulyam equal to those three times iṣṭa-phala-dam gives the desired fruit sadyaḥ at once anavadye O blameless one dhṛtam when held śrī Śrī bhavānī Bhavānī śaṅkara and Śaṅkara devatābhyaḥ to the deities namaḥ salutation kṣamā-yācana-pūrvaka-prārthanam a prayer with a plea for forgiveness samarpayāmi I offer

In this world of birth with its fevers and sickness, crying out in the three pains, bound fast by the snares of children, wife and wealth, blind with pride, laden with sins — Lord Mṛtyuñjaya, dear to Pārvatī, Lord of all, protect me always with your compassionate glance. I contemplate Mṛtyuñjaya, his feet caressed by Pārvatī's lotus hands, in the jewelled palace strewn with fresh lotus petals, spread with lovely white silk, lit by camphor lamps, on a pair of fine pillows. Whoever worships with devotion, at dawn, noon and night, within and without, with these forty-four offerings, reaches the wondrous state of Mṛtyuñjaya. Seeing the liṅga of Umā's lord at dawn gives heaven; at noon, the fruit of a horse-sacrifice; at dusk, liberation; the five-syllable worship at sunset in the pradoṣa hour gives at once, faultless, the fruit of all three. — I offer prayer, asking forgiveness.

catuścatvāriṃśadupacāra pūrvaka samasta rājopacāra śaktyupacāra
bhaktyupacāra pūjayā ca bhagavān sarvātmakaḥ śrī bhavānī śaṃkara devatā
suprīta ssuprasanno varado bhavatu ||
|| sarvaṃ śrīparameśvarārpaṇamastu ||

mantra-hīnam lacking in mantra kriyā-hīnam lacking in rite bhakti-hīnam lacking in devotion sadāśiva O Sadāśiva yat whatever pūjitam worship has been done mayā by me deva O god paripūrṇam complete tat that astu may it be te for you anayā by this śrīmat-ādya-śaṅkara-bhagavat-pāda-viracita composed by the venerable Ādi Śaṅkara catuḥ-catvāriṃśat-upacāra-pūrvaka with its forty-four services samasta-rāja-upacāra all royal honours śakti-upacāra services as one is able bhakti-upacāra-pūjayā worship with services of devotion ca and bhagavān the blessed sarva-ātmakaḥ Self of all śrī-bhavānī-śaṅkara-devatā the deity Śrī Bhavānī-Śaṅkara su-prītaḥ well pleased su-prasannaḥ most gracious vara-daḥ and granting boons bhavatu may he be sarvam all śrī-parama-īśvara-arpaṇam an offering to the supreme Lord astu may it be

Whatever I have worshipped, Sadāśiva, lacking in mantra, in rite, in devotion — may it be complete, O god. By this worship with the forty-four offerings composed by Śrī Ādi Śaṅkara Bhagavatpāda, with all royal offerings, and with offerings as my means and devotion allow, may the Lord, Self of all, Śrī Bhavānī-Śaṅkara, be pleased, gracious and bountiful. All is offered to the Supreme Lord.

|| iti śrī śivapūjāvidhiḥ ||

iti thus ends śrī-śiva-pūjā-vidhiḥ the rite of the worship of Śrī Śiva

Thus the worship of Śrī Śiva.

Śrī Śivārghya mantrāḥ · arghya on Mahāśivarātri ↑

On Mahāśivarātri, after the night's worship, three special arghyas are offered with flowers, akṣata and a coin, and the coins with a gift are given to a brahmin.

gaurīvallabha deveśa trinetra śaśibhūṣaṇa |
sarvapāpaviśuddhyarthaṃ gṛhāṇā'rghyaṃ namo'stu te ||
iti prathamārghyaṃ samarpayāmi ||
|| 1 ||

word by word · translation

gaurī-vallabha beloved of Gaurī deva-īśa lord of gods tri-netra three-eyed śaśi-bhūṣaṇa moon-adorned sarva-pāpa-viśuddhi-artham for cleansing from all sin gṛhāṇa accept arghyam the water of welcome namaḥ salutation astu be te to you iti with this prathama-arghyam the first water of welcome samarpayāmi I offer

Beloved of Gaurī, lord of the gods, three-eyed, moon-adorned — for the cleansing of all sins accept this arghya; salutation to you. — I offer the first arghya.

vyomakeśa namaste'stu vyomātman vyomarūpiṇe |
nakṣatrarūpī bhagavan gṛhāṇā'rghyaṃ namo'stu te ||
iti dvitīyārghyaṃ samarpayāmi ||
|| 2 ||

word by word · translation

vyoma-keśa whose hair is the sky namaḥ salutation te to you astu be vyoma-ātman whose self is the sky vyoma-rūpiṇe whose form is the sky nakṣatra-rūpī whose form is the stars bhagavan O blessed one gṛhāṇa accept arghyam the water of welcome namaḥ salutation astu be te to you iti with this dvitīya-arghyam the second water of welcome samarpayāmi I offer

Salutation to you, sky-haired, whose self and form is the sky, Lord in the form of the stars; accept this arghya, salutation to you. — I offer the second arghya.

māghamāse site pakṣe caturdaśyāṃ mahāniśi |
liṃgodbhavasya velāyāṃ gṛhāṇā'rghyaṃ namo namaḥ ||
iti tṛtīyārghyaṃ samarpayāmi ||
|| 3 ||

word by word · translation

māgha-māse in the month of Māgha site in the bright pakṣe fortnight caturdaśyām on the fourteenth day mahā-niśi at dead of night liṅga-udbhavasya of the arising of the liṅga velāyām at the hour gṛhāṇa accept arghyam the water of welcome namaḥ namaḥ salutation again and again iti with this tṛtīya-arghyam the third water of welcome samarpayāmi I offer

In the month of Māgha, on the fourteenth of the fortnight, in the great night, at the hour when the liṅga arose, accept this arghya; salutation, salutation. — I offer the third arghya.

Pradakṣiṇā · how many rounds ↑

ekā caṃḍyā raveḥ sapta tisraḥ kāryā vināyake |
hareścatasraḥ kartavyāḥ śivasyārdha pradakṣiṇā ||

word by word · translation

ekā one caṇḍyāḥ for Caṇḍī raveḥ for the Sun sapta seven tisraḥ three kāryāḥ are to be done vināyake for Vināyaka hareḥ for Hari catasraḥ four kartavyāḥ are to be done śivasya for Śiva ardha-pradakṣiṇā a half circumambulation

One round for Caṇḍī, seven for the sun, three for Vināyaka, four for Hari, and half a round for Śiva.
